Thanks for the context @tnn-simon. You're right that Secret.data is explicitly documented as storing arbitrary data encoded as base64, which means non-UTF-8 bytes are a completely valid use case validating them out in kubelet would be a breaking change for legitimate workloads.
Given @BenTheElder's comment about re-relaxing the gRPC validation, I think the correct fix is at the gRPC/protobuf layer rather than in makeEnvironmentVariables(). I'll hold off on writing code until @dims or @liggitt weigh in on the preferred direction.

Env var spec
  * Values may contain binary data but must not contain a null byte (disallowing the null byte means that environment variables _already_ cannot handle all values that could be stored in a secret, and we should improve detecting / handling that scenario more gracefully)

Env var handling
  * Depending on the pipeline the value is going through, binary values may or may not be transmitted successfully or losslessly

CRI
  * Binary data in env values was _always_ disallowed by the cri-api spec (it specs the envvar value as a `string` which is defined as being utf-8)
  * Binary data was _accidentally_ allowed on the encoding side (in the kubelet) by missing validation in gogo protobuf
  * Starting in 1.34, the kubelet switched to use standard protobuf encoding library, which strictly validated
  * Whether binary data was supported in a _particular_ container runtime depended on what proto library they used and whether it validated according to the cri-api proto definition as a string


Options I see:
1. Change cri-api from `string value` to `bytes value`. This serializes identically in proto but drops the utf-8 requirement.
   * This moves kubelet behavior back to match pre-1.34 behavior.
   * Whether a particular container runtime or pipeline will actually support binary values with fidelity is still unclear.
   * Still need to validate and reject null bytes in values in the kubelet, which means arbitrary binary data still cannot be reliably placed in Secrets for use as envvars.
   * 1.34, 1.35, 1.36 kubelets will still error on non-utf-8 data (I think the cri-api and kubelet change to treat values as `[]byte` is too invasive to backport)

2. Validate all env values are utf-8 and don't contain the NUL byte, error in the kubelet if they are not, and document a recommendation to do application-level encoding/decoding of binary values to pass through envvars (like base64 encoding, etc).
   * This is more consistent with envvar portability recommendations (from https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/000095399/basedefs/xbd_chap08.html: `For values to be portable across systems conforming to IEEE Std 1003.1-2001, the value shall be composed of characters from the portable character set (except NUL and as indicated below)`).
   * Stays consistent with cri-api spec of the value as a string
   * Stays more consistent with 1.34, 1.35, 1.36 behavior
   * Guides implementers to approaches that are more likely to work with any container runtime and pipeline

~~I think I'm in favor of keeping the cri-api as-is, and preventing propagation of envvar values with non-utf8 or nul bytes in the kubelet~~

edit: hmm... if previously successful pods+containers are now failing on 1.34+, and we can restore this minimally, maybe we should go the route of making the cri-api []byte

Do you have safeguards in your use of binary data in secrets in envvar values to ensure no NUL bytes are present?
while digging around for this I also noticed that none of the ConfigMap → Env transforms pull from the ConfigMap BinaryData field ... that feels worth tracking in an issue to at least document

opened a speculative PR at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139168 for the cri-api change to allow values to be binary to recover 1.34+ compatibility, will discuss with API and node folks there

Thanks @liggitt for the thorough analysis and #139168. I also noticed your comment about ConfigMap.BinaryData not being plumbed through to env vars would it be useful to open a tracking issue for that?
Yes, if only to document the current behavior. I have a hard time seeing us automatically starting to pull configmap binary data into envvars in a non-disruptive way at this point

It is possible to set and retrieve binary non-utf8 data in envvars even via the command line:
```sh
export FOO=$'\x80'

echo -n "$FOO" | hexdump

0000000 0080                                   
0000001
```

however, NUL bytes in envvar values don't seem persistable / usable:

```
export FOO=$'\x80\x00\x80'

echo -n "$FOO" | hexdump
0000000 0080                                   
0000001
```

The Kubernetes 1.33 nodes that support these secrets:
>kubeletVersion: v1.33.7
>containerRuntimeVersion: containerd://2.0.0

The Kubernetes 1.34 nodes that do not support these secrets:
>kubeletVersion: v1.34.6
>containerRuntimeVersion: containerd://2.0.0

Both node pools have the following settings in common:
>architecture: amd64
>kernelVersion: 6.6.130.1-3.azl3
>osImage: Microsoft Azure Linux 3.0
GKE has begun recommending and auto-migrating to a bugfix in the 1.34 minor that changes this behavior (in our case, 1.34.7), so more people may be running into this soon.
ACK -- @liggitt, @samuelkarp and I are at GKE. There are PRs in flight for this. The containerd PRs are close I think, and the Kubernetes PRs are in.

Summarizing the current state:
* Kubernetes release branches / patch versions fix the kubelet side in these versions: v1.34.9+, v1.35.6+, v1.36.2+
* k8s.io/cri-api library is fixed in these versions: v0.34.10+, v0.35.7+, v0.36.3+
* containerd [fixes](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pulls?q=+is%3Apr+author%3Aliggitt+cri-api+envvar) are merged (but not yet released): will be in v2.2.7+, v2.3.4+ (versions prior to v2.2.x were unaffected)
* cri-o [fixes](https://github.com/cri-o/cri-o/pulls?q=+is%3Apr+author%3Aliggitt+envvar) are merged (but not yet released): will be in v1.34.11+, v1.35.6+, v1.36.3+ (versions prior to v1.34.x were unaffected)
thanks @liggitt for the summary !

I also opened PRs with an e2e exercising pods running using binary data in secrets at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pulls?q=is%3Apr+139172+envvar+label%3Aarea%2Ftest

The e2e is currently red, since we're waiting for containerd v2.3.4 to release and be pulled in by `kind`, so the container runtime used in those e2e tests includes the fix.

Last update is that the e2e test I added to make sure pods like this can start successfully passes with the fixed containerd version (verified on 1.34/1.35/1.36 and master)

I'll merge the e2e test for 1.38, but this should be resolved now with latest kubelets and latest CRI patch releases for containerd and cri-o
